subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: When an existing cron quarantine sidecar exceeds the 8 MiB cap, should OpenClaw preserve cron persistence by retaining only one rolling archive and starting fresh, or should it reject the write to preserve all quarantine history?
rationale: The proposed recovery path deliberately trades historical quarantine retention for continued persistence; tests can validate either implementation but cannot decide the intended operational contract.

options.title: Accept bounded rolling recovery
options.body: Keep the fixed single archive and fresh-sidecar behavior, treating older quarantine entries as replaceable diagnostic state.

options.title: Fail the write at the cap
options.body: Reject cap-saturated writes so existing quarantine history remains intact, accepting that cron persistence will require operator remediation.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded rolling recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed single archive and fresh-sidecar behavior, treating older quarantine entries as replaceable diagnostic state.
